# Corpus Anatomy Atlas

> Open educational human anatomy atlas featuring 74 illustrated study chapters, 1,586 documented anatomical structures, 40 microscopic tissue lenses, a 206-bone skeletal inventory, and 312 muscles.

## Core Sections
- [Interactive Atlas Home](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/): Interactive body map, layered human anatomy showcase, and Corpus AI Assistant.
- [Interactive Body Map](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/body-map/): Anterior and posterior clickable human organ map.
- [All 74 Organs & Chapters](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/all-organs/): Complete searchable index of 74 chapters and 1,586 structures.
- [Male Anatomy](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/male-anatomy/): Full-body male surface landmarks, internal organs, and pelvic floor.
- [Female Anatomy](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/female-anatomy/): Full-body female surface landmarks, internal organs, and pelvic floor.
- [Interactive Anatomy Quiz](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/anatomy-quiz/): 446 multiple-choice and visual spot-identification questions.
- [Deep Anatomy Study Path](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/deep-anatomy-study-path/): 17 advanced microanatomy and neurovascular chapters.
- [Anatomy Study Guides Hub](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/): Full index of 74 long-form anatomical & physiological study guides.
- [Anatomy Blog & Study Articles](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/blog/): In-depth educational articles, cranial nerve tables, and physiological guides.
- [About & Editorial Policy](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/about.html): Educational scope, citation standards, and contact information.
- [Privacy Policy](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/privacy-policy/): Privacy and cookie disclosure.

## Published Blog Articles
- [Human Heart Layers, Chambers, Valves & Conduction Paths](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/blog/heart-layers-chambers-conduction/): Explore the human heart wall layers, four chambers, atrioventricular and semilunar valves, coronary arteries, and the SA-to-Purkinje electrical conduction.
- [12 Cranial Nerves (CN I–XII): Nuclei, Foramina & Guides](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/blog/cranial-nerves-1-12-guide/): Study all 12 cranial nerves (CN I–XII) in order with brainstem nuclei, skull base foramina, sensory and motor modalities, parasympathetic paths, and tests.

## All 74 Anatomy Study Guides
- [Heart (Cor)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/heart-anatomy/): Two synchronized muscular pumps in one organ: four chambers, four one-way valves, coronary arteries, and the intrinsic SA-to-Purkinje electrical pacemaker.
- [Lungs (Pulmones)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/lung-anatomy/): Twenty-three generations of branching airways lead to hundreds of millions of elastic alveoli where inspired air meets pulmonary capillary blood across 0.5 µm.
- [Brain (Encephalon)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/brain-anatomy/): Folded cerebral lobes, white-matter commissures, deep thalamic and basal nuclei, cerebellum, and brainstem circuits floating in protective cerebrospinal fluid.
- [Kidney (Ren)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/kidney-anatomy/): Retroperitoneal filtration powerhouses: outer renal cortex, medullary pyramids, calyces, and a million nephrons that purify blood plasma and balance body water.
- [Liver (Hepar)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/liver-anatomy/): Fed by both the nutrient-rich portal vein and oxygen-rich hepatic artery, the liver's hexagonal lobules synthesize proteins, detoxify blood, and secrete bile.
- [Stomach & intestines (Gaster et intestina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/digestive-tract-anatomy/): A continuous muscular digesting and absorbing tube from the acid-churning stomach through the villus-lined small intestine to the water-reclaiming colon.
- [Eye (Oculus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/eye-anatomy/): A self-focusing optical globe: transparent cornea and crystalline lens bend light onto a ten-layered neural retina packed with rod and cone photoreceptors.
- [Ear (Auris)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/ear-anatomy/): Three connected compartments in the temporal bone convert airborne pressure waves into cochlear nerve signals while tracking head rotation and gravity.
- [Pancreas (Pancreas)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/pancreas-anatomy/): A dual-function retroperitoneal gland: exocrine acini secrete bicarbonate and digestive enzymes into the duodenum while endocrine islets regulate blood glucose.
- [Spleen (Lien (splen))](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/spleen-anatomy/): Tucked beneath the left ribs, the spleen pairs immune white-pulp lymphoid follicles with filtering red-pulp cords that recycle aging red blood cells.
- [Thyroid gland (Glandula thyroidea)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/thyroid-and-parathyroid/): Wrapped like a butterfly around the upper trachea, thyroid follicles store iodinated thyroglobulin colloid to pace basal metabolism, with four parathyroids behind.
- [Urinary bladder (Vesica urinaria)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/urinary-bladder-anatomy/): A compliant three-layered detrusor muscle reservoir lined by stretchable transitional urothelium, guarded by a smooth trigone and dual urethral sphincters.
- [Skin (Cutis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skin-anatomy/): Our largest organ combines a self-renewing stratified epidermis with a collagen-rich dermis housing sweat glands, hair follicles, blood vessels, and touch nerves.
- [Spinal cord (Medulla spinalis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/spinal-cord-anatomy/): Protected inside the vertebral canal, a butterfly core of gray-matter neuron horns is surrounded by ascending sensory and descending motor white-matter tracts.
- [Male reproductive system (Organa genitalia masculina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/male-reproductive-system/): Temperature-regulated testes, coiled epididymal maturation ducts, muscular vas deferens, accessory glands, and the shared urogenital tract in complete context.
- [Female reproductive system (Organa genitalia feminina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/female-reproductive-system/): Cyclic follicle maturation in the ovaries, ciliary transport along the uterine tubes, a hormonally dynamic uterus and cervix, vaginal canal, and external vulva.
- [Male body — anterior (Corpus masculinum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/male-surface-anatomy/): Standard anatomical position on the anterior male figure: palpable bony landmarks, muscular contours, and body-wall regions mapped to underlying internal viscera.
- [Female body — anterior (Corpus femininum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/female-surface-anatomy/): Standard anatomical position on the anterior female figure: thoracic, abdominal, pelvic, and limb surface landmarks connected to deeper organ systems.
- [Nervous system — overview (Systema nervosum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/nervous-system-anatomy/): One integrated signaling web: the central brain and spinal cord compute while 12 pairs of cranial nerves and 31 pairs of spinal nerves link every tissue.
- [Nervous system — male (Systema nervosum (vir))](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/male-nervous-system/): Whole-body central and peripheral nerve pathways on the male figure, highlighting limb plexuses alongside prostatic, cavernous, and pudendal pelvic nerves.
- [Nervous system — female (Systema nervosum (femina))](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/female-nervous-system/): Whole-body central and peripheral nerve pathways on the female figure, highlighting limb plexuses alongside uterovaginal autonomic and pudendal pelvic nerves.
- [Cranial nerves (Nervi craniales I–XII)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cranial-nerves-anatomy/): Twelve paired nerves (CN I–XII) emerge directly from the forebrain and brainstem, passing through skull-base foramina to serve special senses, face, and viscera.
- [Autonomic nervous system (Systema nervosum autonomicum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/autonomic-nervous-system/): The involuntary balance between thoracolumbar sympathetic fight-or-flight chains, craniosacral vagal and pelvic parasympathetic rest-and-digest outflow, and gut plexuses.
- [Breast (Mamma / Glandula mammaria)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/breast-anatomy/): Mammary glandular lobules and converging lactiferous ducts supported by fibrous Cooper ligaments over the pectoral fascia, with key axillary lymphatic drainage.
- [Skeleton (Systema skeletale)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/human-skeleton-anatomy/): All 206 named adult bones—80 axial and 126 appendicular—plus compact osteons, spongy trabecular struts, red marrow cavities, and major joint families.
- [Muscular system (Systema musculare)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/muscular-system-anatomy/): Over 300 named skeletal muscle records and 32 tendon pathways across 13 body regions, showing origins, insertions, nerve supply, and sliding-filament action.
- [Lymphatic system (Systema lymphoideum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/lymphatic-system-anatomy/): One-way lymphatic capillaries, filtering cervical, axillary, and inguinal node chains, the thoracic duct, thymus, and spleen working together for fluid and immunity.
- [Vascular system (Systema cardiovasculare)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/vascular-system-anatomy/): High-pressure elastic and muscular arteries branching from the aorta paired with valve-guarded veins and portal circuits returning blood to the heart.
- [Endocrine system (Systema endocrinum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/endocrine-system-anatomy/): Hormone-secreting glands—hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroids, adrenals, pancreas, and gonads—communicating through bloodstream feedback loops.
- [Joints & ligaments (Articulationes et ligamenta)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/joint-classification/): How fibrous sutures, cartilaginous symphyses, and fluid-lubricated synovial capsules balance smooth anatomical motion with ligamentous joint stability.
- [Shoulder joint (Articulatio humeri)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/shoulder-joint-anatomy/): Why the shallow ball-and-socket glenohumeral joint achieves 360-degree reach, stabilized by the fibrocartilaginous labrum and four SITS rotator cuff tendons.
- [Upper airway (Via aerea superior)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/upper-airway-and-larynx/): Warming nasal conchae, the three-part pharynx, and the nine cartilages of the larynx that protect the lower airway during swallowing and vibrate vocal folds.
- [Bone marrow & blood (Medulla ossium)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/bone-marrow-anatomy/): Inside spongy trabecular bone, pluripotent hematopoietic stem cells generate millions of oxygen-carrying red cells, immune leukocytes, and platelets every second.
- [Male pelvis & perineum (Pelvis masculina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/male-pelvis-anatomy/): Sagittal and perineal views of the male pelvis: bladder neck, walnut-sized prostate, rectum, levator ani muscular sling, and pudendal neurovascular canals.
- [Female pelvis & perineum (Pelvis femina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/female-pelvis-anatomy/): Sagittal and perineal views of the female pelvis: bladder, anteverted uterus, vesicouterine and rectouterine pouches, levator ani floor, and perineal body.
- [Uterus — layers & cavity (Uterus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/uterus-anatomy/): From the dome-like fundus to the internal os: how the cyclic endometrium, thick smooth-muscle myometrium, and spiral arteries remodel across life stages.
- [Cervix — transformation zone (Cervix uteri)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cervix-anatomy/): The collagen-dense lower neck of the uterus, where mucus-secreting columnar endocervical epithelium meets squamous ectocervix at the transformation zone.
- [Ovary & uterine tube (Ovarium et tuba uterina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/ovaries-and-fallopian-tubes/): Follicular waves and corpus luteum formation in the ovarian cortex paired with the fimbriae, wide ampulla, and ciliated mucosa of the fallopian tube.
- [Vagina — walls & fornices (Vagina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/vagina-anatomy/): A distensible fibromuscular canal lined by glycogen-rich stratified squamous epithelium, recessed around the cervix into anterior, lateral, and posterior fornices.
- [Vulva — external genital anatomy (Vulva)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/vulva-anatomy/): Honest surface anatomy of the external female genital region—mons pubis, labia majora and minora, clitoral glans, and separate urethral and vaginal openings.
- [Pelvic support & surgical planes (Fascia et ligamenta pelvis feminae)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/pelvic-floor-and-ligaments/): How the tonic levator ani muscular dome, cardinal and uterosacral ligaments, and endopelvic fascial planes suspend pelvic organs above the urogenital hiatus.
- [Testis & epididymis — microanatomy (Testis et epididymis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/testis-and-epididymis/): Inside the fibrous tunica albuginea: 250 testicular lobules, coiled seminiferous tubules, Sertoli blood-testis barrier, rete testis, and epididymal maturation.
- [Prostate, ducts & penis (Prostata et penis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/prostate-gland-anatomy/): McNeal's peripheral, central, and transition zones of the prostate surrounding the prostatic urethra where seminal vesicle and vas deferens ducts converge.
- [Clitoral erectile complex (Clitoris · corpora cavernosa et bulbi vestibuli)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/clitoral-complex-anatomy/): Beyond the visible glans: the internal clitoral body, paired diverging crura anchored to the ischiopubic rami, vestibular bulbs, and dorsal sensory nerves.
- [Penile erectile tissue (Corpora cavernosa · corpus spongiosum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/penile-erectile-anatomy/): Three cylindrical vascular columns—paired dorsal corpora cavernosa and the ventral urethra-bearing corpus spongiosum—wrapped in tough tunica albuginea and Buck fascia.
- [Skin layers & appendages (Epidermis · dermis · tela subcutanea)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skin-layers-microanatomy/): Five epidermal keratinocyte strata, interlocking dermal papillae, reticular collagen bundles, eccrine and sebaceous glands, and specialized touch corpuscles.
- [Facial nerve · CN VII (Nervus facialis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/facial-nerve-anatomy/): Tracing Cranial Nerve VII from the pons through the temporal bone canal and parotid gland to its five facial expression branches, chorda tympani taste, and tear fibers.
- [Trigeminal nerve · CN V (Nervus trigeminus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/trigeminal-nerve-anatomy/): Tracing Cranial Nerve V from the trigeminal ganglion into ophthalmic (V1), maxillary (V2), and mandibular (V3) sensory territories plus the muscles of chewing.
- [Eye · microscopic layers (Bulbus oculi · tunicae oculi)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/eye-layers-and-chambers/): Microscopic architecture of the three ocular coats: five-layered cornea, aqueous humor flow from ciliary processes to Schlemm's canal, and zonular lens suspension.
- [Retina · neural microanatomy (Retina neurosensorialis · epithelium pigmentosum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/retina-anatomy/): How light traverses ten transparent neural layers to trigger rod and cone phototransduction, bipolar-to-ganglion processing, and high-acuity foveal vision.
- [Nephron · kidney microanatomy (Nephron · corpusculum renale)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/nephron-anatomy/): From the fenestrated glomerulus and podocyte filtration slits through the proximal tubule, countercurrent loop of Henle, macula densa, and collecting duct.
- [Brachial plexus · arm nerves (Plexus brachialis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/brachial-plexus-anatomy/): How spinal nerve roots C5–T1 braid into trunks, divisions, and cords to form the musculocutaneous, axillary, radial, median, and ulnar nerves of the upper limb.
- [Cerebrum · cortex & deep pathways (Cortex cerebri · substantia alba · nuclei basales)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cerebral-cortex-and-basal-ganglia/): Coronal deep-brain architecture: six-layered neocortex, corpus callosum, internal capsule projection highway, caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, and thalamus.
- [Meninges, CSF & venous sinuses (Meninges · liquor cerebrospinalis · sinus durae matris)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/meninges-and-cerebrospinal-fluid/): Three protective meningeal membranes (dura, arachnoid, pia), buoyancy-providing cerebrospinal fluid from choroid plexuses, and dural venous sinus drainage.
- [Brainstem & cerebellar circuitry (Truncus encephali · cerebellum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/brainstem-and-cerebellum/): Midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata nuclei, corticospinal pyramidal decussation, and the three peduncles linking the brainstem to the cerebellar cortex.
- [Pulmonary acinus · gas-exchange barrier (Acinus pulmonis · alveoli)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/pulmonary-acinus-and-alveoli/): Inside the terminal respiratory unit: flat Type I pneumocytes, surfactant-secreting Type II cells, alveolar macrophages, and the 0.5-micron blood-air barrier.
- [Hepatic lobule · liver microanatomy (Lobulus hepatis · acinus hepatis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/hepatic-lobule-anatomy/): Hexagonal liver micro-units where portal vein and hepatic artery blood flows inward across fenestrated sinusoids to the central vein while bile flows outward.
- [Small intestine · wall & enteric plexuses (Tunicae intestini tenuis · plexus enterici)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/small-intestine-wall-anatomy/): Four gastrointestinal wall tunics, absorptive villi with central lacteals, stem-cell crypts of Lieberkühn, and the submucosal and myenteric enteric nerve plexuses.
- [Skull & facial bones (Ossa cranii et faciei)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skull-and-facial-bones/): Complete osteology of all 22 adult skull bones—8 cranial vault bones and 14 facial bones—paired with anterior surface and medial sagittal cutaway views.
- [Teeth · dental anatomy (Dentes permanentes et decidui)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/tooth-anatomy-guide/): Interactive Universal (#1–32 / A–T) and FDI two-digit dental charts, four tooth classes, enamel-dentin-pulp layers, periodontal ligaments, and V2/V3 nerves.
- [Anatomical language · planes & movement (Terminologia anatomica)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/anatomical-planes-and-directions/): The universal coordinate system of medicine: standard anatomical position, sagittal, coronal, and transverse planes, directional pairs, and joint movements.
- [Body cavities · regions & quadrants (Cavitates et regiones corporis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/body-cavities-and-regions/): Mapping dorsal and ventral body cavities, double-layered serous membranes, and patient-oriented four abdominal quadrants and nine clinical surface regions.
- [Cells & four basic tissues (Cellulae et textus fundamentales)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cells-and-four-tissues/): How cell organelles and the four fundamental human tissues—epithelial sheets, connective matrix, contractile muscle, and excitable neurons—build every organ.
- [Sperm cell · anatomy & production (Spermatozoon et spermatogenesis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/sperm-cell-anatomy/): How a streamlined 55-micrometer cell packs a haploid nucleus, enzyme-filled acrosome, mitochondrial midpiece, and propulsive flagellum to carry paternal DNA.
- [Egg cell · oocyte & ovulation (Oocytus secundarius et ovulatio)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/egg-cell-anatomy/): Inside one of the body's largest cells: the secondary oocyte, protective zona pellucida, nourishing corona radiata, cortical granules, and ovulation timing.
- [Fertilization · sperm meets oocyte (Fecundatio)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/human-fertilization/): From sperm capacitation and the acrosome reaction in the uterine tube ampulla to the fast cortical block against polyspermy and diploid zygote formation.
- [Zygote to blastocyst · early divisions (Segmentatio et blastocystis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cleavage-and-blastocyst/): Rapid mitotic cleavage without cell growth transforms the single-celled zygote into a compact 16-cell morula and a fluid-filled blastocyst ready to hatch.
- [Implantation · blastocyst in endometrium (Implantatio blastocystis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/blastocyst-implantation/): How the hatched blastocyst anchors to the receptive uterine endometrium, differentiates into cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast, and forms a bilaminar disc.
- [Placenta · maternal–fetal exchange (Placenta et membranae fetales)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/placenta-anatomy/): Branching chorionic villi, the maternal intervillous blood space, and the three-vessel umbilical cord exchange oxygen and nutrients without mixing bloodstreams.
- [Embryo · early organ formation (Embryogenesis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/embryonic-development/): Weeks three to eight: gastrulation establishes ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm as the neural tube closes, somites segment, and major organ systems take shape.
- [Fetus · growth & pregnancy trimesters (Periodus fetalis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/fetal-development/): From week nine to birth: trimester growth, surfactant maturation in developing lungs, and the three fetal circulatory shunts that bypass the lungs and liver.
- [Labor stage 1 · cervix dilates (Partus prima periodus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/first-stage-of-labor/): Rhythmic myometrial contractions pull the collagen-rich cervix upward, thinning (effacing) and dilating the cervical canal to a full ten centimeters.
- [Labor stage 2 · birth of baby (Partus secunda periodus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/second-stage-of-labor/): From complete cervical dilation to birth: how the fetus flexes, rotates, and extends through the curved maternal pelvis and levator ani muscular sling.
- [Labor stage 3 · delivery of placenta (Partus tertia periodus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/third-stage-of-labor/): After the baby is born, interlacing uterine muscle fibers contract like living ligatures to constrict spiral arteries and cleanly deliver the placenta.
